newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria needs privatisation, economic panel says.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria needs privatisation, economic panel says.

text.p: The committee overseeing an economic programme launched by military ruler General Sani Abacha in October has agreed that privatisation of loss-making state firms is the key to developing Nigeria's economy.

"What we are trying to do is to see how the private sector could be prepared for the task ahead to avoid any pitfalls in the implementation," committee member Isaac Aluko-Olokun, quoted by the News Agency of Nigeria on Thursday, told reporters in the capital Abuja.
The programme -- "Vision 2010" -- is modelled on those of Asian nations, notably Malaysia.

The government is trying to revive an economy mired in recession since the annulment of a 1993 poll to restore democracy. It set a gross national product growth target of 5.5 percent this year, but many experts say Nigeria really needs to begin privatisation to stimulate growth.
"Privatisation should be done in a coherent manner so that it will benefit a majority of Nigerians. We do not substitute public monopoly with private monopoly," Aluko-Olokun said.

The Vision 2010 committee, which is expected to deliver its plan by September, is made up of managing directors of multinational oil firms in Nigeria, as well as government officials, bankers, businessmen and traditional rulers.
